report:
Comments on a note are in place: the owner and the accounts a note is shared with can comment on it and list its comments, oldest first. `yarn verify` passes (34 test suites, 190 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `63b9ef5`, not pushed.

**How it works**
- **Where comments live:** inside the Notes context, as an aggregate of their own beside the note (`src/Contexts/Notes/Domain/Comment/`). Who may comment is exactly who may read the note, and whether it's archived is the note's own state, so a separate context would only have to ask Notes both questions on every request.
- **Who decides:** `Note.comment(by, text, now)` checks the rules and then creates the comment. Anyone other than the owner or an account the note is shared with gets "not found". An archived note gets `ArchivedNoteCannotBeCommented`. The note itself doesn't change and isn't saved; only the comment is saved, and it records a `CommentWrittenEvent`, which nothing listens to yet.
- **The text:** required, surrounding spaces trimmed, at most 500 characters. Refusals are `CommentTextRequired` and `CommentTextTooLong`.
- **The API:**
  - `POST /notes/{id}/comments` answers 202; the outcome's `result` is the comment id. Anonymous callers get 403.
  - `GET /notes/{id}/comments` answers 200 with `[{ id, authorId, text, createdAt }]`, oldest first, archived notes included. It answers 404 when the caller can't read the note and 403 when anonymous.
- **Tests and records:** a domain spec (`Comment.spec.ts`) and an end-to-end spec (`comment.routes.e2e.spec.ts`). The decision is written up in ADR 0007 and linked from `docs/adr/README.md` and `src/Contexts/README.md`.

**Decisions I made where the brief was unclear**
- **Not a new context:** I didn't create a separate Discussion context. ADR 0007 records why and when to revisit it.
- **Trimming:** text that is only spaces counts as missing, and the 500-character limit applies after trimming, the same way note titles work.
- **Order of checks:** "not found" comes before "archived", which comes before checking the text. A non-reader therefore never learns that a note is archived.
- **Small race window:** the archived check isn't locked against the comment being saved. A comment sent at the same instant the note is archived, or the commenter's access is removed, can still be accepted. Preventing that would mean putting comments inside the note's version, so every comment would compete with the owner's edits. ADR 0007 records this, as ADR 5 does for the note quota.
- **Readable after losing access:** an account that is no longer a reader can't list the comments either. Its own past comments stay on the note.
- **What comments can't do yet:** they can't be edited or deleted, and they don't notify anyone, because the brief asks for neither.

Note history is in: every edit of a note's title or text keeps what it replaced, and the owner can list and restore those versions. `yarn verify` passes (36 test suites, 202 tests) and the work is committed as `383d04e` on the current branch, not pushed.

**How it works**
- **Where versions live:** on the note itself, as an oldest-first `history` list. Each entry has its number, title, text and `replacedAt`. Because the history is saved together with the edit, an edit can't succeed without its old content being kept.
- **Numbering:** version 1 is the note as first written, and each edit adds the next number. The current content isn't in the list until an edit replaces it. A refused edit keeps nothing.
- **Restoring:** `Note.restoreVersion` follows the same rules as an edit:
  - Only the owner can do it. An account the note is shared with gets `NotAllowed`, and anyone else gets `NotFound`.
  - An archived note is refused with `NoteArchived`, the same error an edit gets.
  - A version the note doesn't have is refused with `NoteVersionNotFound`.
  - When it succeeds, the content it replaces becomes the next version, and it records the usual `NoteEditedEvent` with an extra `restoredVersion` field.
- **The API:**
  - `GET /notes/{id}/versions` answers 200 with `[{ version, title, text, replacedAt }]`, most recent first. It answers 404 for anyone but the owner (including accounts the note is shared with) and 403 when anonymous.
  - `POST /notes/{id}/versions/{version}/restore` answers 202, with an `ERROR` outcome when refused.
- **Tests and records:** a domain spec (`NoteHistory.spec.ts`) and an end-to-end spec (`version.routes.e2e.spec.ts`). The decision is in ADR 0008, linked from `docs/adr/README.md` and `src/Contexts/README.md`.

**Decisions I made where the brief was unclear**
- **Is the current content a version?** No. A note that has never been edited lists `[]`, and asking to restore the current content's number gets `NoteVersionNotFound`.
- **Edits that change nothing still count.** An edit, or a restore, that leaves the content unchanged still adds a version. "Every time a note is edited" doesn't say otherwise.
- **Malformed version numbers** in the URL, such as `latest`, `0` or `1.5`, still get the 202 and then a `NoteVersionNotFound` outcome rather than a 400, the same way malformed tags are handled.
- **Archived notes:** their versions can still be listed. The brief only blocks restoring them.
- **Two meanings of "version":** the product's "version" is a past content, and the note's own `version` field is the counter that stops two simultaneous writes from both winning. I named the stored list `history` to keep them apart.
- **ADR numbering:** I numbered the new ADR 8. Some comments in `src/Architecture` say "ADR 8" and "ADR 25", but those point to the upstream reference repository, not to this project's `docs/adr`.
- **Cost:** a note grows with every edit, and every load reads its whole history. ADR 0008 says when to move the history into an aggregate of its own.

Editors are in: when the owner shares a note they can now choose `reader` (the default) or `editor`, and an editor can write in the note. `yarn verify` passes (38 test suites, 215 tests) and the work is committed as `6c7809e` on the current branch, not pushed.

**How it works**
- **Roles:** the note keeps `editors` as a list next to `sharedWith`, and every editor is also in `sharedWith`. The role is checked by the domain, so anything other than `reader` or `editor` gets an `InvalidShareRole` outcome (still a 202).
- **Sharing again changes the role.** The old `NoteAlreadyShared` refusal is gone. Sharing again in the same role succeeds and changes nothing. Sharing in another role switches it, and the share event now carries the role.
- **What an editor can do:** edit the title and text, restore a version, list the versions, and comment.
  - A reader who tries to edit or restore is refused as `NotAllowed`.
  - An editor who tries anything else the owner does (archive, restore the note, pin, tag, share, set a reminder) is refused as `NotAllowed`.
  - Anyone the note isn't shared with gets `NotFound`, as before.
- **Archived notes:** an editor is refused (`NoteArchived`) just as the owner is.
- **Who made each edit:** every version now has `editedBy`, the account whose edit replaced it, and the edit event carries it too.
- **The API:**
  - `GET /notes/{id}` gains `editors` in the owner's answer.
  - `GET /notes/{id}/versions` now answers the owner and editors, with `editedBy` on each version. A reader gets 404, as a stranger does.
- **Tests and records:** a new domain spec (`NoteEditors.spec.ts`) and end-to-end spec (`editor.routes.e2e.spec.ts`), with the existing specs updated. The decision is in ADR 0009, ADR 0008 now notes that editors can list versions too, and both READMEs are updated.

**Decisions I made where the brief was unclear**
- **What an editor sees of the note:** the same as a reader, without `sharedWith` or `editors`. Only the owner sees who the note is shared with.
- **Editor order:** `editors` follows the order of `sharedWith`, not the order people became editors.
- **Order of checks when sharing:** owner, then archived, then role, then "not the owner", then whether the account exists. Changing a role is refused on an archived note, like any sharing.
- **Readers refused an edit get a different message** from readers refused other actions ("only the owner or an editor"). The type is still `NotAllowed` in both cases.
- **Versions made before this feature:** I didn't migrate any stored history, because storage is in memory and starts empty.
- **No unsharing:** nobody can be removed from a note yet; an editor can only be turned back into a reader. The brief doesn't ask for unsharing, and ADR 0009 notes the gap.

A person can now delete their own account with `DELETE /accounts/me`, and their data goes with it. `yarn verify` passes (42 test suites, 225 tests) and the work is committed as `b047ac4` on the current branch, not pushed.

**How it works**
- **Security** removes the account. That alone covers three of the requirements:
  - **Tokens:** a token they hold now makes the request anonymous, because sign-in already checks the account still exists. `GET /accounts/me` answers 403.
  - **Login:** their email gets 401.
  - **Signing up again:** the email is free, and creates a new account with a new id.
- **One new event, `AccountDeleted`,** is published to the other contexts with only the account id and the time, no email. Each context then erases its own part:
  - **Notes:**
    - The notes they own are deleted with their versions and shares, and any pending reminder is cancelled.
    - All comments on those notes are deleted, along with their comments on other people's notes.
    - Other people's notes stop listing them in `sharedWith` and `editors`.
  - **Notifications:** all of theirs are deleted.
  - **Plans:** their plan is removed. An account that never switched plan has nothing to remove.
- **Delivered more than once:** each erasure finds nothing the second time.
- **Tests and records:** a domain spec (`AccountDeparture.spec.ts`), unit specs for the Notifications and Plans reactions, and an end-to-end spec (`account-deletion.routes.e2e.spec.ts`) covering the whole scenario. The decision is in ADR 0010, linked from both READMEs.

**Gaps you should know about**
- **The person can't see the outcome of their own deletion.** Once it succeeds their token is anonymous, so the operation-tracking endpoint answers 403. The 202 is their answer, and the token stopping working is the outcome.
- **Erasure isn't instant.** For a moment after the 202, people the notes were shared with can still see them. The end-to-end test waits for this.
- **A failed erasure isn't retried.** If someone saves a note shared with the departing account at the same instant, that context's whole erasure fails. The failure is visible in the operation tracker, but nothing re-runs it until the event is delivered again.
- **A note can be left without an owner.** If the person had a command already running when the account was removed, such as a note being written, it can land after their notes were erased.

**What stays, by my decision**
- **`editedBy` on other people's notes:** past versions still carry the departed account's id. It's only an id that now names nobody, and the history belongs to the note's owner.
- **Notices sent to other people,** such as "a note shared with you was archived," stay with those people.
- **Operation records** in the tracker aren't erased; the brief doesn't list them.

Search works: `GET /notes/search?q=…` returns the notes you can read whose title or text holds every word of the query. `yarn verify` passes (44 test suites, 232 tests), and the work is committed as `10a7135` on the current branch, not pushed.

**How it works**
- **The query:** `SearchWords` splits `q` on whitespace, lowercases it and drops repeated words. If no word is left (missing, empty or only spaces), the search is refused with `SearchQueryRequired`, which answers 400. An anonymous caller gets 403, checked before the query.
- **Which notes:** your own and those shared with you, whether as reader or editor. Archived notes are left out; a restored note comes back into results.
- **The answer:** 200 with `[{ id, title, ownerId }]`, most recent first by creation date.
- **Tests:** a domain spec (`SearchWords.spec.ts`) and an end-to-end spec (`search.routes.e2e.spec.ts`).
- **Docs:** I updated the Notes line in `src/Contexts/README.md`. I wrote no ADR, because search adds no context and no relationship between contexts.

**Decisions I made where the brief was unclear**
- **Words can be split between title and text.** I read "its title or its text contains every word" as each word appearing in either one. So "groceries eggs" finds a note titled "Groceries" whose text mentions eggs. The stricter reading, where all the words must be in the title or all in the text, would not match it. If you want the stricter reading, it's a one-line change in `SearchWords.matches`.
- **"Contains" means part of a word too.** "grocer" matches "Groceries", and "milk" matches "milkshake".
- **Order:** "most recent" means most recently created, the same as the other note lists. It doesn't follow the latest edit.
- **No paging:** results aren't paginated or limited. The search scans every note in memory, which is fine at this size; a real store would want a full-text index.
